reading.stem: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks:
Dear Friends of Westbank Shelter,
During the last storm, our staff placed every available blanket in the old kennels to keep the animals dry. We now have drawings for a roof that will give the twelve outdoor kennels a permanent cover. A building firm has offered to supply the labor, provided we can buy the materials. We are asking supporters to contribute whatever amount they can toward the cost of that roof. The shelter office will issue a receipt for each gift and report the total in our next newsletter. Thank you for considering the animals in our care.
The Westbank Shelter Team
choices: 폭풍 기간 동안 보호소를 비우라고 안내하려고
동물 보호소의 견사 지붕 자재비를 후원해 달라고 요청하려고
유기 동물 입양 심사의 기준을 설명하려고
evidence: We are asking supporters to contribute whatever amount they can toward the cost of that roof.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 글의 목적
시공 인력은 업체가 제공하기로 했고 필요한 것은 자재비이다. 편지는 지붕 마련을 위한 금전적 후원을 요청한다.
근거 “We are asking supporters to contribute whatever amount they can toward the cost of that roof.”

reading.stem: 다음 글에 드러난 주인공의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: The last surfer had gone in when David spotted a dark fin a short distance beyond his board. It cut the water once, vanished, and appeared nearer. His mouth went dry. He kept the board between himself and the shape as he paddled steadily toward shore. Only when the water fell below his knees did he risk looking back. The fin remained far beyond the breaking waves. His feet pressed into firm sand, and the tight knot under his ribs began to loosen. He sat beside his towel until he could laugh at how hard he was breathing.
evidence: His feet pressed into firm sand, and the tight knot under his ribs began to loosen.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 심경 변화
물속의 지느러미를 보며 두려워하지만 모래 바닥에 발을 디디고 안전해지자 가슴의 긴장이 풀린다.
근거 “His feet pressed into firm sand, and the tight knot under his ribs began to loosen.”

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: “Why can't you keep your desk as tidy as your sister's?” sounds like a request about a desk. To the child hearing it, it may sound like a public ranking of two children. The comparison offers neither a place for loose pencils nor an explanation of when the desk must be clear. It can, however, give the child a new reason to resent the sister. Tell the child what the task requires and notice progress against that requirement. When correcting one child, describe the desired behavior without using a sibling as the standard.
choices: 정리 능력을 비교할 때는 가족 전체의 순위를 공개해야 한다.
한 아이를 지도할 때는 형제와 비교하지 말고 원하는 행동을 구체화해야 한다.
아이의 자존감을 위해 규칙을 설명하는 일을 피해야 한다.
형제간 경쟁을 줄이려면 한 아이의 과제를 다른 아이에게 맡겨야 한다.
아이들 사이의 모든 갈등은 집안일의 양을 같게 하면 해결된다.
evidence: When correcting one child, describe the desired behavior without using a sibling as the standard.
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 필자의 주장
비교는 정리 방법을 알려 주기보다 형제에 대한 반감만 키울 수 있다. 필요한 행동과 진전을 직접 말하라는 주장이다.
근거 “When correcting one child, describe the desired behavior without using a sibling as the standard.”

reading.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>a fence without a sign</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: Every Friday the bakery staff left one shelf empty until noon. An old delivery once arrived late, and the open shelf had saved time. Years after the supplier changed, new workers were still corrected for using the space. Nobody could point to a written instruction. The empty shelf was <u>a fence without a sign</u>: people walked around it because they had always seen others do so. Written rules can at least be brought to a meeting and examined. An unspoken custom may restrict action for years because nobody thinks to question its original purpose.
choices: a physical obstacle created by a late delivery
a warning whose meaning everybody has discussed
a flexible suggestion that never affects work
an invisible habit that continues to limit choices
a recent order that lacks anyone willing to enforce it
evidence: An unspoken custom may restrict action for years because nobody thinks to question its original purpose.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 함축 의미
말 없는 울타리는 이유가 사라져도 암묵적인 규칙처럼 선택을 제한하는 관습이다. 빈 선반을 남겨 두던 배경이 변했다는 점에 주목한다.
근거 “An unspoken custom may restrict action for years because nobody thinks to question its original purpose.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: The first promise of January was to swim for an hour every weekday. By the second week it had collided with two late buses and an evening meeting. A different promise, to pack the swimming bag on Sunday and swim ten minutes on Tuesday, left fewer opportunities for the plan to collapse. Ten minutes will not accomplish every fitness goal. It can, however, become something a person actually repeats, and the amount can grow from there. A small action repeated reliably makes a stronger starting point for a lasting habit than an impressive plan rarely carried out.
choices: 습관을 빨리 만들려면 실패할 때마다 운동량을 두 배로 늘려야 한다.
지속할 습관은 실행하기 어려운 큰 계획보다 반복할 수 있는 작은 행동에서 출발한다.
계획을 자세히 세우는 일은 습관 형성에 언제나 방해가 된다.
처음 정한 운동 시간은 익숙해진 뒤에도 바꿔서는 안 된다.
같은 행동을 반복하면 운동 효과는 반드시 사라진다.
evidence: A small action repeated reliably makes a stronger starting point for a lasting habit than an impressive plan rarely carried out.
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 글의 요지
작은 수영 계획은 반복 가능성이 높고 나중에 늘릴 수도 있다. 크기보다 실제로 지속할 수 있는 시작이 중요하다.
근거 “A small action repeated reliably makes a stronger starting point for a lasting habit than an impressive plan rarely carried out.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Sitting on a bus, a composer may hear an entire imaginary orchestra without anybody in the next seat noticing. Something changes when she writes the opening bars and asks a violinist to try them. The sound that seemed easy in her head may require a different bow movement; the player's response can lead to a phrase she had never imagined. Imagination supplies possibilities, but a creative work comes into being through engagement with a medium. Creativity begins to be visible when imagined possibilities are put to work in a particular activity.
choices: the movement from private imagining to creative practice
the need to finish every composition before playing a note
the role of silence in preventing original thought
the advantage of keeping all musical ideas secret
differences in ticket prices for live and imagined concerts
evidence: Creativity begins to be visible when imagined possibilities are put to work in a particular activity.
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 글의 주제
상상은 혼자 품을 수 있지만 창작은 글이나 연주처럼 구체적인 분야에서 구현하며 발전한다. 작곡가와 연주자 사례가 이를 보여 준다.
근거 “Creativity begins to be visible when imagined possibilities are put to work in a particular activity.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A sports reporter can tell a story in the order she experienced it: the early clouds, the arriving teams, the doubtful first minutes, and eventually the winning goal. A reader rushing to work may leave after the first paragraph and never find out who won. A news report therefore often begins with what the reader most needs to know. Later paragraphs can recover the drama, add quotations, or explain a disputed call. Putting the result first allows even a reader who stops early to take away the essential news. This order serves the reader rather than the clock.
choices: Reporting a Match Without Interviewing Anyone
Why Sports News Should Always Follow the Clock
The Best Way to Hide a Match Result
Why the Final Score Belongs at the Beginning
How a Long Report Can Replace the Scoreboard
evidence: Putting the result first allows even a reader who stops early to take away the essential news.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 글의 제목
시간순 서술에서는 중간에 읽기를 멈추면 결론을 놓친다. 핵심 결과를 앞에 두는 뉴스 구성의 이유를 담은 제목이다.
근거 “Putting the result first allows even a reader who stops early to take away the essential news.”

reading.stem: 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

title: Homes Choosing Gas for Winter Heating
blocks.note: Case study data for this exercise.

blocks: The chart shows the percentage of homes using gas as their main heating fuel in five sample districts.
choices: One of the two figures for Field was below 40%, and the other was above it.
For 2023, Forest ranked second highest among the five categories.
For 2018, the figure for Marsh exceeded that for Forest by 4 percentage points.
The two bars for Bridge are 25 percentage points apart.
For Harbor, the figure for 2023 was above the figure for 2018.
evidence: Harbor: 18, 61
Bridge: 35, 60
Forest: 38, 12
Marsh: 42, 69
Field: 27, 65
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 도표 내용 불일치
2023의 다섯 값을 내림차순으로 배열하면 Forest(12%)의 순위는 5위이다.
[지문 근거] “Harbor: 18, 61” / “Bridge: 35, 60” / “Forest: 38, 12” / “Marsh: 42, 69” / “Field: 27, 65”

reading.stem: Carol Ryrie Brink에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
blocks: Stories told by Carol Ryrie Brink's grandmother did more than entertain her. The grandmother raised the girl after she lost her parents, and the stories later fed her imagination as an author. She and her husband, a mathematics professor, spent several years in France. Her first novel appeared in 1934; just two years later, Caddie Woodlawn earned the Newbery Award. Although readers often associate her with children's literature, her work included fiction and nonfiction, and her audience extended to adults.
choices: 부모를 잃은 후 할머니 손에서 자랐다.
evidence: her audience extended to adults
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 내용 불일치
그녀의 독자층에는 성인도 포함되었다.
[지문 근거] “her audience extended to adults”

reading.stem: Museum Detectives Day에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

blocks.title: Museum Detectives Day
lines: lead
Spend a morning following clues from one display case to another. A museum educator will help each group design a final clue for the next group.
sub
After the activity, families must collect children at the side entrance.
sub
The program is for children aged eight to eleven.
sub
A snack is supplied during the morning break.
sub
Bring a pencil; notebooks will be handed out.
sub
The final clue will be written in a small group.

choices: 연필을 가져와야 하고 공책은 나누어 준다.
활동 후 보호자는 정문에서 어린이를 데려간다.
evidence: families must collect children at the side entrance
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 안내문 내용 불일치
보호자가 아이를 데려가는 곳은 정문이 아니라 옆문이다.
[지문 근거] “families must collect children at the side entrance”

reading.stem: Basement Bands Concert에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

blocks.title: Basement Bands Concert
lines: lead
Three local bands share the stage beneath the old cinema. Each will play a short set, with a break before the final performance.
sub
Seats are not assigned; choose any empty chair on arrival.
sub
The doors open fifty minutes before the first set.
sub
Tickets must be bought in advance.
sub
Soft drinks are sold in the lobby only.
sub
Please leave large bags in the free lockers.

choices: 큰 가방을 보관할 때 사물함 요금을 내야 한다.
첫 연주를 시작한 뒤에 문을 연다.
도착한 뒤 비어 있는 의자를 선택할 수 있다.
공연 시작 후에만 표를 구매할 수 있다.
evidence: Seats are not assigned
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 안내문 내용 일치
좌석 지정이 없으므로 도착한 관객이 빈자리를 고를 수 있다.
[지문 근거] “Seats are not assigned”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3점]
blocks: A researcher can teach a rat ① <u>press</u> a lever by making a small food reward follow the action. The first press may occur by accident. What makes the event useful for the experimenter ② <u>is</u> the change in the chance of another press later. A lever ③ <u>connected</u> to a recording device allows each press to be counted without interrupting the animal. By ④ <u>changing</u> the delay before food appears, the researcher can investigate how strongly the animal links the reward to ⑤ <u>what</u> it has just done.
evidence: teach a rat
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 어법
teach는 목적어 뒤에서 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취한다. teach a rat press가 아니라 teach a rat to press가 되어야 한다.

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3점]
blocks: An old family album is labeled simply “Photographs,” even though every picture in it lacks color. For the first owner, contrasting black-and-white pictures with color ones may have been ① <u>unnecessary</u>. Only when a new alternative becomes familiar does the earlier form often acquire a more ② <u>specific</u> name. A similar shift occurs when an instrument that once had only one form gains a new version. What used to require no modifier then becomes ③ <u>indistinguishable</u> in speech through the addition of a descriptive word. The new label helps listeners ④ <u>identify</u> the intended version and makes the earlier contrast ⑤ <u>explicit</u>.
evidence: the addition of a descriptive word
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임
종류를 구분하는 수식어가 붙으면 말로도 해당 형태를 구별할 수 있게 된다. indistinguishable 대신 distinguishable이 맞다.
[지문 근거] “the addition of a descriptive word”

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: A student replaces a scratched desk with a bright new one. The old chair, perfectly comfortable the previous day, suddenly looks shabby beside it. A new chair then draws attention to a faded lamp. None of these objects has become less useful, and the student did not set out to furnish the whole room. One purchase has changed the standard by which the other objects are seen. The chain of spending is driven by a desire for <blank/>, because the student wants the objects to appear to belong together.
evidence: the student wants the objects to appear to belong together
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 빈칸 추론
책상 구입 뒤 기능에 문제가 없던 물건도 조화를 이루지 못해 보인다. 연쇄 구매를 부른 것은 물건 사이의 일관성을 맞추려는 욕구다. 근거 표현은 “the student wants the objects to appear to belong together”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: A printing company loses a major contract. At the first meeting a manager suggests selling the large press immediately. A colleague asks for two days to find out whether a different publisher wants the same size of print run. Keeping the machine for forty-eight hours costs little; buying it back after a sale would cost a great deal. Waiting is not a refusal to decide. In this situation it is a way to <blank/> before an expensive choice becomes final. A little time may supply information that an immediate vote cannot.
choices: guarantee that the lost contract will return
preserve an option while uncertainty can be reduced
increase the resale price by delaying every sale
avoid being responsible for any later decision
prove that a slow decision is always more accurate
evidence: A little time may supply information that an immediate vote cannot
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 빈칸 추론
적은 대기 비용으로 새 수요를 확인하고 되돌리기 어려운 결정을 피할 수 있다. 기다림이 늘 정답이라는 일반화는 아니다. 근거 표현은 “A little time may supply information that an immediate vote cannot”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: On the night before a difficult audition, Leo volunteers for a task that will keep him awake late. He genuinely wants the part and knows the task will weaken his performance. Why accept it? If he sings badly after a full night of sleep, he may have to wonder about his ability. After a sleepless night he can blame his fatigue. The choice sacrifices a chance of success in exchange for protection from a particular interpretation of failure. In effect, Leo is <blank/> before the result is known. The obstacle can later serve as his explanation.
choices: showing that he no longer cares about the part
testing whether his voice improves with less sleep
arranging an excuse that leaves his ability untested
making the audition conditions fairer for other singers
collecting evidence that extra practice harms performance
evidence: The obstacle can later serve as his explanation
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 빈칸 추론
피곤함을 실패의 탓으로 돌릴 여지를 미리 만들어 가창 능력 자체에 대한 평가를 피하려는 자기방해다. 근거 표현은 “The obstacle can later serve as his explanation”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: An art class studies a photograph for half a minute. Asked what is in it, several pupils say that a fisherman is disappointed. The instructor asks them to point to disappointment on the paper. They point instead to a lowered head, an empty net, and a boat at the edge of the frame. A different story could account for the same details. Their first response may be reasonable, but they cannot assess it until they <blank/>. The second description separates what the photograph supplies from what the viewers add.
choices: identify the visible details behind their interpretation
agree on the private intention of the photographer
reject every emotional reaction to a photograph
learn the complete history of the fishing village
choose the explanation that most classmates prefer
evidence: separates what the photograph supplies from what the viewers add
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 빈칸 추론
낙담했다는 해석과 숙인 머리·빈 그물이라는 관찰을 구분해야 해석을 점검할 수 있다. 근거 표현은 “separates what the photograph supplies from what the viewers add”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
blocks: People considering an unfamiliar concert may look at its reservation page before they listen to a sample. ① Concert halls often number upper-floor seats differently from seats on the ground floor. ② A long list of bookings can make an undecided visitor think that earlier listeners knew something worth knowing. ③ Her booking then lengthens the list that the next visitor sees. ④ The growing display may therefore persuade later customers even if they have no direct evidence about the performance. ⑤ Here the visible decisions of others become a reason for making the same decision.
evidence: the visible decisions of others become a reason for making the same decision
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 흐름과 무관한 문장
예매 수가 선택의 근거가 되고 다음 사람의 판단에 누적 영향을 준다는 사회적 증거의 원리다. 좌석 번호 체계는 무관하다. 근거 표현은 “the visible decisions of others become a reason for making the same decision”이다.

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: At a library desk, two readers kept moving the same lamp. One tipped it toward a large map; the other immediately tilted it away.

Turning the glossy page to a different angle allowed the map reader to keep the bright light. A compromise about the position of the lamp had failed because its position was never the thing either reader ultimately wanted.
The librarian first tried placing the lamp halfway between them. Neither reader liked the compromise, so she asked what each adjustment was intended to achieve.
Their answers revealed different needs. One reader wanted to make out tiny place names; the other needed to stop reflected light from hiding the words on a glossy page.
evidence: Their answers revealed different needs
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 글의 순서 (2점)
(B) - (C) - (A)의 순서이다. 중간 지점이라는 타협이 실패해 이유를 묻고, 서로 다른 필요가 드러나며, 종이 각도를 바꿔 두 필요를 함께 충족한다.
[지문 근거] “Their answers revealed different needs”

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: A town reported that most residents supported a fund for repairing unsafe buildings. A later survey seemed to show that support had collapsed within a week.
She therefore asked the town to repeat both versions on the same day with comparable groups. That comparison would give wording a fairer test than a story about a sudden change of public mind.
Both descriptions referred to the same plan, yet one made its benefit prominent and the other its cost. The reporter could not tell how much of the apparent decline had actually occurred.
Before looking for a political event that could explain the fall, a reporter obtained both questionnaires. The first had called the proposal a safety fund and the second a charge on property owners.
evidence: Both descriptions referred to the same plan
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 글의 순서 (3점)
(C) - (B) - (A)의 순서이다. 상이한 두 질문의 표현을 확인한 뒤 같은 계획의 이익과 비용에 서로 주목시켰음을 설명하고 표현 효과를 시험하는 재조사를 제안한다.
[지문 근거] “Both descriptions referred to the same plan”

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
blocks: It tried to put that particular uncertainty in someone else's hands by signing a fixed-price contract.

A school did not know exactly how much the repairs to its roof would cost. ( ① ) Under this arrangement, the builder rather than the school would pay if the materials turned out to be more expensive than expected. ( ② ) The school still had a different uncertainty to consider: would that builder finish the work on time? ( ③ ) A low price on a signed document would offer little comfort if the pupils returned before the roof was safe. ( ④ ) Checking the builder's previous work could reduce this second risk, though it could never remove it completely. ( ⑤ ) Passing one risk to another party had changed what the school needed to investigate.
evidence: Under this arrangement

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3점]
blocks: A moving belt was introduced to overcome that remaining delay.

Workers assembling a radio once walked back and forth collecting separate pieces for each unit. ( ① ) A supervisor arranged the pieces in the order they were needed and gave each worker a single station. ( ② ) The team produced more radios, but half-finished sets still waited for someone to carry them to the next station. ( ③ ) With the carrying now done by the belt, each worker could concentrate on attaching one component as the radio approached. ( ④ ) The output increased again, this time without any worker becoming faster at attaching a component. ( ⑤ ) Both changes improved the process by removing travel, but they removed travel from different parts of the job.
evidence: With the carrying now done by the belt

정답 ③ · 문장 삽입 (3점)
작업대 간 운반이 여전히 지연을 일으킨다는 문제 뒤에 벨트를 도입하고 다음 문장에서 운반을 벨트가 맡은 효과를 설명한다.
[지문 근거] “With the carrying now done by the belt”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A cafeteria wanted more customers to drink water. It kept the same prices and continued selling every drink it had sold before. Instead of adding posters about healthy living, the manager put chilled water beside the trays where customers first entered the line. It had previously been available only in a refrigerator beyond the cash register. More people began picking it up. The experiment did not establish that their beliefs about nutrition had changed. It showed that the easier option to notice and reach can attract buyers even while all earlier choices remain available.
Changing the (A) of an option can affect behavior without (B) the alternatives.
evidence: the easier option to notice and reach
all earlier choices remain available

41-42.head: [41~42] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: At a mountain fork, four students spread their maps on a stone. One calculates the distance to every possible shelter, another compares tiny differences in the slopes, and a third wants to finish the comparison before they take a step. Their aim is (a) <u>reasonable</u>: avoid walking into a dead end. But the daylight that would let them read the track is being spent on the calculation. One student proposes a rule established on a previous trip: follow the marked route unless reliable information shows that it is closed. This rule (b) <u>multiplies</u> the number of issues they must address immediately: only one question remains. Does the closure notice cover this trail? The group reads the notice and can (c) <u>proceed</u> without predicting every part of the walk. A simple rule is not always (d) <u>superior</u> to a detailed comparison. Its advantage grows when waiting for another detail imposes a (e) <u>cost</u> greater than the benefit of knowing it.

43-45.head: [43~45] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: When Arun applied for a position at a hotel, the manager asked for a digital portfolio of photographs. Arun explained that (a) <u>he</u> had printed pictures but no computer. The manager handed back the envelope and pointed out a copy shop by the market.

The copy shop was closed. Beside its shutter, a fruit seller was trying to photograph a basket with a phone that had a cracked screen. Arun opened (b) <u>his</u> envelope and showed her how to use reflected light. The seller asked him to come back when the afternoon sun reached the stall.

At the end of the month the hotel manager saw a line outside a bakery and recognized Arun's name under a photograph in the window. When the manager offered (c) <u>him</u> an interview, Arun thanked her. For the moment, (d) <u>he</u> said, the market was keeping him busy.

That afternoon the seller posted the new picture in (e) <u>her</u> online shop. A neighbor wanted pictures too. Arun charged just enough for prints and bus fare, and began keeping a record of which pictures brought customers to each stall.
